title: India-Japan Summit: Modi-Takaichi Sign Defence Pact, Economic Partnership Framework and MoCs on AI, Metals, Energy
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral talks with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, resulting in the signing of a defence pact, an economic partnership framework, and multiple Memoranda of Cooperation (MoC) covering artificial intelligence, critical minerals/metals, and energy. The two leaders also agreed to push for an early Quad meeting. Japan committed to a $10 billion investment package in India as part of the economic framework. Over 100 Japanese firms have expressed interest in India's semiconductor sector through joint ventures and technology partnerships.
exam_angle: India-Japan bilateral relations, the Quad grouping, and critical mineral supply chains are recurring themes in GS Paper 2 (IR). The defence technology transfer aspect (Japan's UNICORN mast stealth technology for Indian warships) is also relevant to GS Paper 3 (Defence).
key_facts: Defence pact + economic partnership framework signed during Modi-Takaichi summit
MoCs signed on AI, metals (critical minerals), and energy
Japan committed $10 billion investment in India
Both PMs agreed to push for early Quad summit
source: The Indian Express / Reuters / Times of India

title: Supreme Court to Examine Whether Habeas Corpus Can Challenge 'Chain Arrests' in Multiple Cases
summary: The Supreme Court of India has agreed to examine whether a habeas corpus petition under Article 32/226 can be used to challenge the practice of 'chain arrests', where an accused is repeatedly re-arrested in different cases immediately upon getting bail, effectively circumventing judicial orders. The case raises fundamental questions about the right to personal liberty under Article 21 and the misuse of the arrest power by investigating agencies. The bench is expected to frame guidelines on this issue.
exam_angle: Habeas corpus as a fundamental writ, Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty), and limits on the power of arrest are core polity/GS Paper 2 topics. Chain arrests as a form of executive overreach vs. judicial oversight is an important contemporary constitutional issue.
key_facts: SC examining if habeas corpus can challenge 'chain arrests'
Chain arrest: re-arresting accused in new cases immediately after bail is granted
Relevant Articles: Article 21 (personal liberty), Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies)
Habeas corpus is one of the five prerogative writs in India

title: Indian Navy MARCOS Foil Piracy Bid in Gulf of Aden, Secure Cargo Ship
summary: The Indian Navy's elite MARCOS (Marine Commandos) successfully foiled a piracy attempt in the Gulf of Aden and secured a cargo ship carrying a critical consignment. This operation is part of India's sustained anti-piracy mission in the western Indian Ocean region under Operation Sankalp. The Gulf of Aden is a strategically vital chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Arabian Sea.
exam_angle: India's maritime security operations in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and the Gulf of Aden are important for GS Paper 3 (Defence) and GS Paper 2 (IR). MARCOS and Operation Sankalp are frequently asked facts.
key_facts: MARCOS = Marine Commandos, the special operations unit of the Indian Navy
Operation Sankalp: India's anti-piracy and maritime security mission in the Arabian Sea/Gulf of Aden
Gulf of Aden connects Red Sea to Arabian Sea — key global shipping lane
Piracy attempt foiled; cargo ship with critical consignment secured

title: Anti-Doping Bill to Be Tabled in Monsoon Session as India Tops Global Doping Violations List Again
summary: India has once again topped the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) list of countries with the highest number of doping violations. In response, the government is set to table the National Anti-Doping Bill (Anti-Doping Bill) during the upcoming Monsoon Session of Parliament. The bill aims to strengthen India's anti-doping framework and align it with international standards set by WADA.
exam_angle: Legislative measures for sports integrity and India's compliance with international anti-doping standards (WADA) are relevant to GS Paper 2 (Governance) and GS Paper 3. WADA and NADA (National Anti-Doping Agency) are frequently tested in current affairs.
key_facts: India topped WADA list of doping violations (again in 2026)
Anti-Doping Bill to be tabled in Monsoon Session of Parliament
WADA = World Anti-Doping Agency; NADA = National Anti-Doping Agency of India
Objective: align India's anti-doping framework with international standards

title: RBI Tells Parliamentary Panel: Cryptocurrency Difficult to Regulate
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) informed a Parliamentary standing panel that cryptocurrency is extremely difficult to regulate due to its decentralised nature and cross-border character. The RBI reiterated its long-standing position that cryptocurrencies pose risks to financial stability and macroeconomic management. This statement comes amid ongoing global and domestic debates on framing a crypto regulatory framework in India.
exam_angle: RBI's stance on cryptocurrency regulation is critical for GS Paper 3 (Economy). The tension between financial innovation and regulatory oversight, and the role of the RBI as a financial regulator, are important exam themes.
key_facts: RBI told Parliamentary panel: cryptocurrency is difficult to regulate
RBI cites decentralised, cross-border nature as key regulatory challenges
RBI has consistently opposed legitimising cryptocurrency as legal tender
India has not yet enacted a dedicated Cryptocurrency Regulation Bill

title: India-UK Free Trade Agreement: Export Orders Rush Ahead of July 15 Rollout
summary: Following the conclusion of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA), Indian exporters are witnessing a significant rush of export orders ahead of its implementation scheduled for July 15, 2026. The FTA is expected to reduce tariffs on Indian goods — particularly textiles, leather, and pharmaceuticals — entering the UK market. However, exporters note that while enquiries from US buyers have increased amid Trump tariff uncertainty, actual order conversions remain limited.
exam_angle: India's bilateral trade agreements, especially the India-UK FTA, are highly exam-relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy). The contrast with US tariff-related uncertainty also provides context for India's trade diversification strategy.
key_facts: India-UK FTA implementation date: July 15, 2026
Key beneficiary sectors: textiles, leather, pharmaceuticals
Export orders rushing ahead of rollout; US enquiries up but orders limited due to Trump tariff uncertainty
India-UK FTA was years in negotiation before conclusion

title: Viksit Bharat-GRAMG Scheme: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay Opposes Centre's Scheme, Flags Rs 5,000 Crore Burden
summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay has written to Prime Minister Modi urging amendment of the Viksit Bharat Guarantee GRAMG (VB-GRAMG) scheme, arguing that it imposes an additional financial burden of Rs 5,000 crore on the state. Karnataka is also preparing for rollout of the scheme. The VB-GRAMG scheme is part of the Viksit Bharat (Developed India) initiative aimed at ensuring last-mile delivery of central government schemes in rural areas.
exam_angle: Centre-state fiscal relations, cooperative federalism, and centrally sponsored schemes are core GS Paper 2 topics. The Viksit Bharat initiative and its implementation dynamics are important for current affairs.
key_facts: VB-GRAMG = Viksit Bharat Guarantee Rural Area Modified/Gram scheme
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay flags Rs 5,000 crore additional burden on state
Karnataka preparing for scheme rollout
Part of broader 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India by 2047) initiative

title: Iran Supreme Leader Khamenei's Death: India's Congress Leader Salman Khurshid, Mehbooba Mufti to Attend Funeral
summary: Following the death of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, India's Congress leader Salman Khurshid confirmed he would represent the Congress party at the funeral, having received an invitation from Iran. Former J&K Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti also announced she would travel to Iran for the funeral proceedings. Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif also planned to attend. Iran issued warnings to the US and Israel against any attacks during the funeral processions.
exam_angle: Iran's political transition after Khamenei — the world's longest-serving supreme leader — has major geopolitical implications for West Asia, India-Iran relations, energy security (Chabahar Port), and the broader regional balance of power (GS Paper 2 IR).
key_facts: Iran Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei passed away (as per these reports)
Salman Khurshid (Congress) to represent party at funeral; Mehbooba Mufti also attending
Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to attend the funeral
India-Iran ties significant due to Chabahar Port and energy imports
source: Reuters / Times of India / Indian Express

title: Pakistan: 125-Year-Old Historic Gurdwara Demolished by Businessman, India Calls It 'Highly Deplorable'
summary: A 125-year-old Gurdwara in Pakistan's Punjab province was demolished by a local businessman, drawing strong protests from the Sikh community. India's Ministry of External Affairs called the demolition 'highly deplorable' and summoned Pakistani authorities. The incident has reignited concerns about the safety and preservation of Sikh and Hindu religious heritage sites in Pakistan.
exam_angle: Protection of minority religious heritage sites in Pakistan is relevant to India-Pakistan relations and India's diaspora diplomacy. India's statements on minority rights in neighbouring countries connect to GS Paper 2 (IR) and also the culture/heritage angle.
key_facts: 125-year-old Gurdwara demolished in Pakistan's Punjab by a businessman
India's MEA termed it 'highly deplorable'
Sikh community in Pakistan protested the demolition
Issue relates to protection of minority religious heritage in Pakistan

title: BHASHINI Showcases Multilingual AI Innovations at NCeG 2026; Launches Rajasthan Language Model Hackathon
summary: BHASHINI, India's national language translation mission under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), showcased its multilingual AI innovations at the National Conference on e-Governance (NCeG) 2026. It also launched the Rajasthan Language Model Training Hackathon to promote regional language AI models. BHASHINI aims to break language barriers in digital service delivery across India's 22 scheduled languages.
exam_angle: BHASHINI is a frequently tested scheme in Prelims — its objectives, parent ministry, and role in digital inclusion are important. It connects to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) and GS Paper 2 (Governance/e-governance).
key_facts: BHASHINI = Bhasha Interface for India (National Language Translation Mission)
Launched by: Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY)
Showcased at NCeG 2026 (National Conference on e-Governance)
New: Rajasthan Language Model Training Hackathon launched

title: Government Sends Notices to WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal Over 'Username' Feature Citing Security Risks
summary: The Indian government (Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology) sent notices to messaging platforms WhatsApp, Telegram, and Signal over their 'username' features, flagging potential risks to national security and user privacy. Meta (WhatsApp's parent) defended the feature arguing it enhances user privacy. The notices are part of India's broader push to ensure compliance of social media intermediaries with the IT Rules 2021.
exam_angle: Regulation of social media intermediaries under IT Rules 2021, the balance between user privacy and national security, and MeitY's oversight powers are critical GS Paper 2 (Governance) and GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Internal Security) topics.
key_facts: MeitY sent notices to WhatsApp, Telegram, and Signal over username features
Concern: anonymous usernames may aid criminal/anti-national activities
Governed by IT Rules 2021 (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code)
Meta (WhatsApp) defended feature as privacy-enhancing

title: Sanoj Kumar Jha (IAS) Assumes Additional Charge as CMD of NLC India Limited
summary: Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha, an IAS officer, has assumed additional charge as Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of NLC India Limited (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation). NLC India Limited is a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Coal, primarily engaged in lignite mining and power generation in Tamil Nadu.
exam_angle: Appointments to key PSE leadership positions and knowledge of Navratna CPSEs are tested in Prelims. NLC India Limited's status as a Navratna CPSE and its role in coal/lignite sector are important facts.
key_facts: Sanoj Kumar Jha (IAS) = new CMD (Additional Charge) of NLC India Limited
NLC India Limited = formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation
Status: Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise
Ministry: Ministry of Coal

title: China Plans New Economic Corridor Through Bangladesh and Myanmar, Bordering India
summary: After establishing the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), China is now reportedly planning a new economic corridor that would pass through Bangladesh and Myanmar, both of which share borders with India. This corridor would be part of China's broader Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) strategy to increase connectivity and influence in South and Southeast Asia. India has consistently raised concerns about BRI projects passing through or near its territory.
exam_angle: China's expanding connectivity projects in India's neighbourhood — CPEC, BRI, and now the Bangladesh-Myanmar corridor — are critical for GS Paper 2 (IR) on India's neighbourhood policy and maritime/land security.
key_facts: China planning new economic corridor via Bangladesh and Myanmar (both bordering India)
Part of China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)
Earlier: CPEC (China-Pakistan Economic Corridor) — India opposes as it passes through PoK
India's concern: encirclement via String of Pearls strategy

title: Global Defence Bank: Canada to Announce 10 Founding Nations Soon
summary: Canada announced that the names of the 10 founding nations of a proposed Global Defence Bank will be revealed shortly. The Global Defence Bank is a new multilateral financial institution being conceptualised to pool resources for defence and security spending among like-minded nations, particularly in the context of growing geopolitical threats. This development is significant in the context of NATO burden-sharing debates and Western efforts to strengthen collective security financing.
exam_angle: New multilateral financial institutions for defence and security represent an emerging trend in global governance, relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR) and international security frameworks. India's potential role as a founding member would be significant.
key_facts: Global Defence Bank: proposed new multilateral institution for defence financing
Canada to announce 10 founding nations imminently
Context: NATO burden-sharing debates and rising global security threats
Concept: pool financial resources for collective defence spending

title: Madras High Court Penalises MEA and MHA Officials Over Delay in Transfer of Narcotics Convict from Sri Lanka
summary: The Madras High Court imposed penalties on officials from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for delays and procedural lapses in the transfer of a narcotics convict from Sri Lanka to India. The case involves provisions of prisoner transfer treaties between India and Sri Lanka. The court's action highlights judicial accountability of executive officials in implementing bilateral legal cooperation agreements.
exam_angle: Inter-country prisoner transfer treaties, MEA-MHA coordination on extradition/transfer matters, and judicial oversight of executive action are relevant to GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance and IR).
key_facts: Madras HC penalised MEA and MHA officials
Issue: delay in transfer of narcotics convict from Sri Lanka to India
India-Sri Lanka prisoner transfer treaty invoked
Highlights judicial oversight of executive action in bilateral legal matters

title: E20 Fuel: Survey Flags Accelerated Wear and Tear in Older Vehicles; Oil Minister Defends Policy
summary: A new survey has found that beyond a drop in fuel mileage, E20 blended petrol (20% ethanol, 80% petrol) is causing accelerated wear and tear in older vehicles not designed for high ethanol content. Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri acknowledged a 'minor' mileage drop but defended E20, citing its use even in racing cars. India's ethanol blending programme is a key component of its energy transition and farmer income support strategy.
exam_angle: India's Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP), the National Biofuel Policy 2018 (revised 2022), and E20 fuel targets (20% blending by 2025) are frequently tested in GS Paper 3 (Economy/Energy/Environment). The debate also touches on consumer impact vs. energy security trade-offs.
key_facts: E20 = 20% ethanol blended with 80% petrol
Survey: E20 causes mileage drop AND accelerated wear in older vehicles
India's EBP target: 20% ethanol blending by 2025 (E20)
Governed by: National Biofuel Policy 2018 (revised 2022)

title: AI-Driven Tech Layoffs: India Second Hardest Hit Globally
summary: According to a new analysis, India is the second hardest-hit country globally in terms of technology sector layoffs driven by artificial intelligence adoption and automation. The trend reflects the displacement of routine and mid-level IT/tech jobs as companies increasingly integrate AI tools for coding, customer service, and data processing. The US remains the most affected country. This has significant implications for India's large IT workforce and skilling requirements.
exam_angle: The impact of AI on employment, India's IT sector, and the need for reskilling/upskilling are important for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech and Economy). The 'future of work' debate connects to India's demographic dividend and human capital development.
key_facts: India = 2nd hardest hit country in AI-driven tech layoffs globally (US is 1st)
AI automation displacing routine IT, coding, customer service, and data jobs
India has one of the world's largest IT/tech workforces (~5 million)
Implications: urgent need for reskilling, upskilling, and new job creation strategies

title: Carlsberg India Files for $700 Million IPO
summary: Carlsberg India, the Indian subsidiary of Danish brewing giant Carlsberg Group, has filed for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) worth approximately $700 million (around Rs 5,800 crore). This would be one of the significant consumer goods IPOs in recent times. Carlsberg entered India in 2006 and operates multiple breweries across the country, with brands including Carlsberg, Tuborg, and Royal Stag (in partnership with Pernod Ricard).
exam_angle: Major IPOs are tracked for GS Paper 3 (Economy) and Prelims current affairs. Foreign company subsidiary IPOs in India reflect capital market development and FDI trends.
key_facts: Carlsberg India files for IPO worth ~$700 million (~Rs 5,800 crore)
Parent company: Carlsberg Group (Denmark)
Key brands: Carlsberg, Tuborg
Carlsberg entered India in 2006; operates multiple breweries
